newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Rivlin--Japan faces tough economic challenge.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Rivlin--Japan faces tough economic challenge.

text.p: Alice Rivlin, Vice Chairman of the Federal Reserve Board, said Japanese monetary and fiscal authorities face a formidable challenge in preserving the nascent Japanese economic recovery.

Speaking to a luncheon meeting of the Institute for International Bankers here, Rivlin said, "The Japanese economy is only slowly and hesitantly emerging from its worst period of economic activity in modern Japanese economic history."

She said it has taken several years for stimulative monetary and fiscal policies to take hold in Japan, adding that major problems in the Japanese banking system have "not yet been completely rectified."

"The monetary and fiscal authorities have a serious challenge in preventing the recovery in Japan from faltering, recognizing that additional financial system restructuring and consolidation may still be necessary," she said.
Japan's recovery is crucial for other economies around the globe, including the U.S., Rivlin said.
"Japanese citizens who care about their success are not the only ones ... The importance of Japan in the world economy means that we all have to care about that success."
